Mansoura, Egypt - Wikipedia
Contents
Mansoura, Egypt
Mansoura
(
Egyptian Arabic
:
المنصورة
,
romanized:
El Manṣūra
,
IPA:
[
el.mɑnˈsˤuːɾɑ
]
,
locally
[
el.mænˈsˤuːɾe
]
;
lit.
'
The Victorious
'
) is a city in
Egypt
located on the eastern bank of the Damietta branch of the
Nile
river.
[
3
]
The city is the capital of the
Dakahlia Governorate
and has an estimated population of 600,000 as of 2024.
[
2
]
Etymology
Mansoura
(
منصورة
) in
Arabic
means 'victorious'. The city is named after the
El Mansoura Battle
(1250) against
Louis IX of France
during the
Seventh Crusade
.
[
4
]
History
Mansoura was established in 1219 by
al-Kamil
of the
Ayyubid dynasty
upon the
Phatnitic
branch of the
Nile
on the site of several older villages, such as Al-Bishtamir (
البشطمير
) and Kafr al-Badamas (
كفر البدماص
, from
Ancient Greek
ποταμός
'river, canal').
[
5
]
[
6
]
After the Egyptians defeated the
Crusaders
during the
Seventh Crusade
, the city was named
Mansoura
.
In the
Seventh Crusade
, the
Capetians
were defeated and put to flight; between fifteen and thirty thousand of their men fell on the battlefield.
Louis IX of France
was captured in the main
Battle of Fariskur
, and confined in the house of Ibrahim Ibn Lokman, secretary of the sultan, and under the guard of the eunuch Sobih. The king's brother was imprisoned in the same house. The sultan provided for their sustenance. The house of Ibrahim Ibn Lokman is now the only museum in Mansoura. It is open to the public and houses articles that used to belong to the French monarch, including his personal thirteenth century
toilet
.
[
7
]
The
Mansoura Air Battle
[
8
]
[
9
]
on October 14, 1973, occurred during the
Yom Kippur War
.
Israeli Air Force
fighters attacking Egyptian air bases were intercepted by the
Egyptian Air Force
. On that day, 160 jet fighters, most of which belonging to Israel, battled for 53 minutes over Mansoura. The Egyptian army claimed that despite the numerical and qualitative superiority of the Israeli warplanes, 17 Israeli planes were downed. (2 according to the Israelis), while the rest retreated.
[
10
]
[
11
]
[
12
]
Egypt announced the loss of six planes, only three of which fell to Israeli fire. The Egyptian government subsequently changed the country's "Air Force Day" from November 2 to October 14, to commemorate the Mansoura Air Battle.
[
9
]
Geography
Mansoura lies on the east bank of the
Damietta
branch of the
Nile
, in the
Delta
region. Mansoura is about 120
km northeast of
Cairo
. Across from the city, on the opposite bank of the Nile, is the town of
Talkha
.
Köppen-Geiger climate classification system
classifies its climate as
hot desert
(BWh).
Culture
The
Egyptian Arabic
dialect spoken by Mansoura's population is a Northern Egyptian Arabic dialect, with noticeable influences from the city's surrounding rural villages, each of which has contributed to the city's population over the years. There are also similarities to
Alexandrian
Egyptian Arabic
in some aspects of pronunciation.
The Mansoura National Museum used to be Dar Ibn Lockman, the house where
Louis IX
was imprisoned in 1250 during the
Seventh Crusade
. Displayed in the museum are the suits of mail and swords of the crusaders, as well as a collection of maps. Huge paintings depict the Battle of Mansoura.
The Mansoura branch of the National Library was inaugurated in 2008 as the Mansoura Misr Library.
[
14
]
Mansoura is famous for its architectural style, especially the Shinnawi Palace (after Mohamed Bek El-Shinnawi, a member of the
Wafd Party
). It was built by an
Italian
architect in 1928. The mosque of El-Saleh Ayoub El-Kebir is one of the most important in Mansoura. It was built by a loyal servant of the Sultan and is located in Al-Sagha Street that separates "Old Mansoura" from the modern city.
[
15
]
Like
Cairo
,
Alexandria
and
Port Said
, Mansoura was home to a flourishing
Greek
community Many of the older and best established shops and businesses around the city still bear their original
Greek
names. Mansoura also had a small Italian population living in the city too. The first Old English school in the city was established on the site of the old
Greek
school in the Toriel area, one of the traditionally relatively affluent residential districts of the city.
Al-Mansoura joined the UNESCO Global Network of Learning Cities in 2025.
[
16
]
Infrastructure
The
University of Mansoura
was founded in 1962, initially as a branch of
Cairo University
.
[
17
]
The
Urology
and
Nephrology
center of
Mansoura University
founded by Prof
Mohammed Ghonem
is considered to be the best kidney center in the Middle East and Africa.
[
15
]
Mansoura has a sports
stadium
(
Mansoura Stadium
) which is home to its
football
team.
